vocabulary.meaning_en: old-fashioned and not stylish (usually about a woman's clothes)
vocabulary.example: Her coat looked a bit dowdy.

vocabulary.meaning_en: stylish and looking good
vocabulary.example: That's a snazzy jacket!

vocabulary.meaning_en: cheap, not sincere, trying too hard and so unpleasant
vocabulary.example: The film had a cheesy ending.

vocabulary.meaning_en: not real or genuine
vocabulary.example: The actors seemed inauthentic.

vocabulary.meaning_en: not honest about your real feelings
vocabulary.example: His smile was insincere.

vocabulary.meaning_en: beautiful in a simple, stylish way
vocabulary.example: We ate at an elegant restaurant.

vocabulary.meaning_en: (slang, about a man) dirty, poor and unattractive
vocabulary.example: He hadn't washed for days and looked dusty.

vocabulary.meaning_en: having achieved a lot, often with money and a good position
vocabulary.example: She is a successful businesswoman.

vocabulary.meaning_en: rich; having a lot of money
vocabulary.example: They live in an affluent area.

vocabulary.meaning_en: disgusting, awful, or rude
vocabulary.example: The shop assistant was nasty to me.

vocabulary.meaning_en: nice, charming and likable
vocabulary.example: We had a pleasant evening.

vocabulary.meaning_en: disgusting or very ugly
vocabulary.example: There's old food under the sofa. Gross!

vocabulary.meaning_en: beautiful, very nice
vocabulary.example: You look lovely today.

vocabulary.meaning_en: too simple and obvious; used too often (jokes, stories)
vocabulary.example: My uncle always tells corny jokes.

vocabulary.meaning_en: worldly and knowing a lot; complex
vocabulary.example: She has sophisticated taste in books.

vocabulary.meaning_en: having experience of the world from travel and reading
vocabulary.example: He is a worldly man who has lived in five countries.

vocabulary.meaning_en: having many details or parts
vocabulary.example: The story is complex and interesting.

vocabulary.meaning_en: cheap, loud and in bad taste
vocabulary.example: The gold plastic decorations looked tacky.

vocabulary.meaning_en: modest and showing good taste
vocabulary.example: Their home is simple and tasteful.

vocabulary.meaning_en: not safe, or possibly dishonest
vocabulary.example: That old bridge looks sketchy.

vocabulary.meaning_en: (British) dishonest, unreliable or possibly dangerous
vocabulary.example: Don't buy a phone from that dodgy shop.

vocabulary.meaning_en: (British) unpleasant or of poor quality
vocabulary.example: We stayed in a grotty little room.

fine_lines.title: cheesy vs corny vs tacky
fine_lines.explanation_ar: cheesy: رخيص وغير صادق ومتكلّف. corny: بسيط جدًا ومستهلك، خاصة النكت. tacky: صاخب وذو ذوق رديء.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Cheesy: cheap and not sincere. Corny: too simple and used too often, especially jokes. Tacky: loud and in bad taste.

examples.sentence: Plastic flowers on the table look tacky.

fine_lines.title: sketchy vs dodgy vs grotty
fine_lines.explanation_ar: sketchy: غير آمن أو مريب. dodgy (بريطانية): غير أمين أو خطير محتمل. grotty (بريطانية): رديء الجودة وكريه.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Sketchy: not safe or dishonest. Dodgy (UK): dishonest, unreliable, maybe dangerous. Grotty (UK): poor quality and unpleasant.

examples.sentence: He sold me a dodgy watch.

expressions.meaning_ar: dowdy ↔ snazzy، cheesy ↔ elegant، dusty ↔ successful/affluent، nasty ↔ pleasant، gross ↔ lovely، corny ↔ sophisticated، tacky ↔ tasteful
expressions.meaning_en: dowdy/snazzy, cheesy/elegant, dusty/affluent, nasty/pleasant, gross/lovely, corny/sophisticated, tacky/tasteful
expressions.example: The hotel wasn't nasty at all; it was very pleasant.

expressions.phrase: You don't have to be nasty.
expressions.example: I only asked a question. You don't have to be nasty.

expressions.phrase: across the pond / the other side of the pond
expressions.meaning_ar: على الضفة الأخرى من المحيط (بريطانيا أو أمريكا)
expressions.meaning_en: on the other side of the Atlantic Ocean (UK or North America)
expressions.example: My cousin lives across the pond in London.

expressions.meaning_en: something very easy that you get for free
expressions.example: The first question was a gimme.

questions.question: What is the opposite of "nasty"?
questions.explanation_en: Pleasant is the opposite of nasty.

questions.question: A joke that is too simple and old is ___.
questions.explanation_en: A corny joke is simple and obvious.

questions.question: The opposite of "tacky" is ___.
questions.explanation_ar: tasteful = ذو ذوق رفيع، عكس tacky.
questions.explanation_en: Tasteful is the opposite of tacky.

questions.question: "The hotel had insects everywhere. It was ___."
questions.explanation_en: A hotel with insects is nasty.

questions.question: "I liked ___ restaurants with excellent food and a great atmosphere."
questions.explanation_en: Elegant restaurants are stylish and nice.

questions.question: Which word is British and means "poor quality and unpleasant"?
questions.explanation_ar: grotty كلمة بريطانية تعني رديء وكريه.

questions.question: "That bridge looks ___. I don't think it's safe."
"Across the pond" (said in Canada) means:
questions.explanation_ar: across the pond تعني الجهة الأخرى من المحيط الأطلسي.
questions.explanation_en: It means the other side of the Atlantic.
